claims.text: Combinatorial thin-film deposition can create a continuous composition spread in the HfNbTaTiZr alloy system.
Systematic deviations from equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will produce predictable changes in local hardness and elastic modulus.
A uniform, equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr thin film produced by conventional sputtering provides the initial state.
Combinatorial sputtering permits controlled variation of individual element percentages across an HfNbTaTiZr film.
Room-temperature nanoindentation mapping can locally assess hardness and elastic modulus across the composition spread.
Variations in elemental concentration change local grain size, phase distribution, and lattice distortion.
Changing element percentages alters solid-solution strengthening in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changing element percentages alters microstructural evolution.
Microstructural evolution can modulate the hardness of HfNbTaTiZr.
Microstructural evolution and solid-solution strengthening modulate the elastic modulus of HfNbTaTiZr.
Increasing the Hf percentage may increase hardness.
The proposed Hf-induced hardness increase results from greater lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening.
Traditional bulk processing averages mechanical properties and obscures the effects of varying individual elements.
Composition-dependent effects are expected to be most evident in thin films tested by nanoindentation.
Results from the proposed thin-film experiment cannot be assumed to transfer directly to bulk materials or tensile strength.
The magnitude of composition-dependent property changes may depend on interactions among multiple elements and microstructural factors.
High-pressure torsion refinement of powder-processed HfNbTaTiZr can produce a very fine microstructure and hardness of 410 HV10.

contradictions.description: The initial state defines the baseline material as a uniform equiatomic thin film made by conventional sputtering, whereas the baseline field defines it as an equiatomic alloy made by traditional bulk processing. These are materially different controls.
